current_text.html: Every church shall elect persons to the offices of ruling elder and deacon in the following manner: At such times as determined by the Session, communicant members of the congregation may submit names to the Session, keeping in mind that each prospective officer should be an active male member who meets the qualifications set forth in 1 Timothy 3 and Titus 1. Nominees for the office of ruling elder and/or deacon shall receive instruction in the qualifications and work of the office. Each nominee shall be examined in: a. his Christian experience, especially his personal character and family management (based on the qualifications set out in 1 Timothy 3:1-7 and Titus 1:6-9), b. his knowledge of Bible content, c. his knowledge of the system of doctrine, government, discipline contained in the Constitution of the Presbyterian Church in America (BCO Preface III, The Constitution Defined), d. the duties of the office to which he has been nominated, and e. his willingness to give assent to the questions required for ordination. (BCO 24-6). In the examination of the nominee's personal character, the Session shall give specific attention to potential notorious concerns. Careful attention must be given to his practical struggle against sinful actions, as well as to persistent sinful desires. The nominee must give clear testimony of reliance upon his union with Christ and the benefits thereof by the Holy Spirit, depending on this work of grace to make progress over sin (Psalm 103:2-5, Romans 8:29) and to bear fruit (Psalm 1:3, Gal. 5:22-23). While imperfection will remain, when confessing sins and sinful temptations publicly, the nominee must exercise great care not to diminish the seriousness of those sins in the eyes of the congregation, as though they were matters of little consequence, but rather should testify to the work of the Holy Spirit in his progress in holiness (1 Cor. 6:9-11). Notwithstanding the above, the Session may render a decision on Christian experience at any point in the process, and based on that decision, may judge him, whether previously ordained or not, ineligible for that election. If there are candidates eligible for the election, the Session shall report to the congregation those eligible, giving at least thirty (30) days prior notice of the time and place of a congregational meeting for elections. If one-fourth (1/4) of the persons entitled to vote shall at any time request the Session to call a congregational meeting for the purpose of electing additional officers, it shall be the duty of the Session to call such a meeting on the above procedure. The number of officers to be elected shall be determined by the congregation after hearing the Session's recommendation.

relationships.title: Requiring ruling elders and deacons to state confessional differences at ordination

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB found the proposed amendment to BCO 24-1 requiring REs and deacons to disclose confessional differences not in conflict with the Constitution.

relationships.title: Session's role in examining officer nominees under BCO 24-1

occurrences.excerpt: Proposed amendment to BCO 24-1 clarifying a session's role in examining officer nominees was found not in conflict with the BCO.
Overture to amend BCO 13-6, 21-4, and 24-1 to mandate background checks for church officers was found not in conflict and adopted 8-0-0.
A second overture (from Ohio Presbytery) to amend BCO 13-6, 21-4, and 24-1 requiring background checks was also found not in conflict and adopted 8-0-0.
The CCB found a South Texas Presbytery overture requiring background checks for church office not in conflict with BCO 13-6, 21-4, and 24-1.
CCB unanimously found South Texas Presbytery's overture mandating criminal background checks for all minister and officer candidates not in conflict with the Constitution.

relationships.title: Proposed additional ordination requirements in BCO 21-4 and 24-1
relationships.disposition: not in conflict; Adopted by the CCB

occurrences.excerpt: CCB advised that Pittsburgh Presbytery's overture adding ordination requirement paragraphs to BCO 21-4 and 24-1 is not in conflict with the Constitution.

relationships.title: Clarifying moral qualifications for ordained office holders

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB found that Eastern Pennsylvania Presbytery's overture amending BCO 21-4 and 24-1 to clarify moral requirements for church office was not in conflict with the BCO, and was adopted.

relationships.title: Disqualifying same-sex attracted men from ordination under BCO 7

occurrences.excerpt: An overture from Westminster Presbytery to amend BCO 7 and related provisions disqualifying same-sex attracted men from ordination was found in conflict and adopted.

relationships.title: Ordination ban for men self-identifying as gay Christians

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB found this overture to amend BCO 17 prohibiting ordination of men using gay-identity labels to be in conflict with existing BCO provisions, though it was adopted.

relationships.title: Session discretion on timing of officer candidate examinations

occurrences.excerpt: An overture to amend BCO 24-1 allowing sessions discretion over the timing of portions of elder and deacon nominee examinations was found constitutionally vague.

relationships.title: Session discretion over timing of officer nominee examinations

occurrences.excerpt: An overture amending BCO 24-1 to clarify that sessions have discretion over the timing of portions of officer-nominee examinations was found not in conflict and adopted.

relationships.title: Election of Ruling Elders and Deacons

occurrences.excerpt: Applying BCO 20-5's large-minority provision to the election of ruling elders and deacons conflicts with BCO 24-1 and 24-3.

relationships.title: Stated Clerk of General Assembly Reporting All Exceptions Taken in All Presbyteries

occurrences.excerpt: The overture was mostly not in conflict with the Constitution, but a final sentence risked eroding presbyteries' authority to determine confessional subscription.

relationships.title: Application of BCO 24-1 to the Reelection of Officers

occurrences.excerpt: BCO 24-1 applies fully to men with no prior official relationship to the church; for men already serving, lower courts determine which provisions apply at re-election.

relationships.title: Setting a nomination deadline before the one-month officer election notice
relationships.disposition: advice given — session may set nomination deadline before one-month meeting notice; all six required elements must be included

occurrences.excerpt: A session may set a nomination deadline before the one-month congregational meeting notice expires, but all six BCO 24-1 requirements for officer election must be met.

relationships.title: Re-examination of previously ordained officer nominees by session
relationships.disposition: advice given — re-examination required; session may find nominee deficient

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB advised that all nominees for ruling elder or deacon, including previously ordained individuals, must be re-examined by the session, which retains the right to find them deficient.

relationships.title: Re-examination and divestiture of officers in rotational systems

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB advised that the BCO provides no procedure for re-examining rotated-off officers' qualifications, but divestiture may only occur under BCO 24-6, 38-2, or 34-10.

relationships.title: Session authority over officer nominees and inactive elders under rotation

occurrences.excerpt: A session must present all qualified nominees for election and may not use BCO 24-6 to exclude inactive officers; presbytery proceedings are not automatically required for long-inactive elders.

relationships.title: Session limiting eligible nominees on officer election ballot

occurrences.excerpt: A session may not withhold qualified nominees from the congregation's ballot to limit board size; BCO 24-1 requires all eligible men to be reported to the congregation.

relationships.title: Rotating sessions, ballot control, and officer election procedures

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB answered five questions on officer elections: the session must present all eligible men, the congregation determines the number elected, and no constitutional limit restricts election frequency beyond a 30-day notice.

metadata.synopsis: The SJC sustained Psiaki’s complaint and held that the CPC Session erred by ordaining and installing officers elected at a February 5, 2023 congregational meeting where the congregation’s bylaw excluded communing members under 18 from voting. Reading BCO 6-4, 25-1, and 25-7 together, the SJC ruled that all communing members are entitled to vote and that local bylaws cannot impose an age restriction; the “good and regular standing” language addresses censure, not age. The decision did not annul the completed ordination/installation, but required future elections and installations to comply with the Constitution.

The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order because BCO 43-1 permits complaints against acts or decisions of church courts, and a congregation is not such a court. metadata.synopsis: The Michelsons’ complaint challenged a congregational meeting’s procedure for electing three assistant pastors as associate pastors—allegedly without a pulpit committee, ballots, counted abstentions, or protection for a substantial minority. The SJC dismissed it as not judicially in order: BCO 43-1 requires complaint against an act or decision of a court, but the complaint attacked congregational actions, while the Session’s only act was calling the meeting and was not objected to. The SJC noted other possible redress; the dissent found the Session’s call and recommendation justiciable.

metadata.synopsis: A minister complained that his presbytery wrongly refused to order a BCO 31-2 investigation into another minister’s Covenant of Works/Federal Vision views. The SJC sustained the complaint and remanded for that investigation, holding that BCO 31-2 requires investigation of credible, injurious reports about Christian character. The presbytery erred by applying the higher evidentiary standard for conviction after process; reports sufficient to trigger investigation need not establish guilt or a strong presumption of guilt, and hearsay or conflicting testimony can require investigation rather than justify refusal. A concurrence agreed in result; the dissent found no clear error in the presbytery’s exercise of discretion.

metadata.synopsis: A presbytery annulled a session's actions after the session added to a petition-called congregational meeting a recommendation that the congregation invoke BCO 24-6 against eleven elders. The SJC sustained the session's complaint: BCO 25-2 permits a session to add agenda items, and BCO 24-6 does not require a member-initiated motion; the congregation's own 503–229 vote began the process. It reinstated the session's actions, declared remaining relief moot, and noted one recorded dissent; no dissent text appears.

relationships.title: Larry Ball v. Westminster Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: A complaint challenged Westminster Presbytery's denial of a challenge to its May 15, 2001 plan to withdraw from the PCA. The SJC answered no: the Presbytery did not err, and denied the complaint. BCO 25's local-church withdrawal right and the BCO Preface's grassroots principles extend to presbyteries unless expressly excluded, so a presbytery may determine its own membership and affiliation. The plan did not 'act for' local churches; they retained rights to remain in the PCA or leave, and retained property and internal operations.

relationships.title: Parks et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: Complainants challenged a Session plan under which most elders voluntarily resigned, the Session granted severance and benefits to its former pastor, proposed about a year with an interim pastor before a permanent call, and contemplated revising local bylaws. The SJC denied all four items. It held that the BCO permitted jointly considered voluntary resignations, that severance concerned resignation and the budget rather than a pastoral call, and that the plan and bylaw proposal were not themselves unconstitutional. Any later call still had to follow the BCO without undue delay, and local bylaws had to remain consistent with it.

topics: fundamentals of the system of doctrine
suspension from office without due process
metadata.synopsis: Bowen challenged Presbytery’s attempt, two years after installation, to rescind its earlier ruling and annul local officers’ elections and ordinations without trial. The SJC sustained the complaint: ordination is perpetual, deposition requires judicial process, and rescission was out of order after implementation; Presbytery likewise could not suspend a local elder without due process. But it affirmed that infant baptism and limited atonement are fundamentals admitting no officer exception. The officers remained in office but doctrinally out of accord; voluntary demission or proper process was advised.

relationships.title: Chappell v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery

topics: suspension of session without due process
metadata.synopsis: Ruling Elder Chappell complained against Eastern Carolina Presbytery's Commission, which had suspended the session of Fuller Memorial Presbyterian Church and constituted itself as a 'Session Pro Tem' without due process or congregational consent. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the BCO grants no authority for a presbytery to depose a session and act in its place, that suspension requires due process, and that the congregation has an inalienable right to be governed by officers it has chosen.

relationships.title: Marshall v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery

topics: suspension of session without due process
metadata.synopsis: Teaching Elder Wallace Marshall complained against the same Eastern Carolina Presbytery actions at Fuller Memorial Presbyterian Church that were the subject of Case 90-4, filed separately as a Teaching Elder complainant. The SJC sustained this complaint on essentially the same grounds as Case 90-4, finding that the presbytery lacked authority to suspend the session without due process and to constitute itself as a 'Session Pro Tem.'
